title: Docetaxel 75 mg/m² · previously treated NSCLC

agents.name: Docetaxel
agents.explanation: Docetaxel stabilises tiny structures called microtubules. Cells need these to separate their chromosomes during division; disrupting the process can stop cancer cells multiplying. Healthy dividing cells are also affected.
agents.watch: Take prescribed steroid premedication. Report fever, lasting numbness, swelling, sore nails or infusion symptoms.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and sepsis
Hair loss, mouth soreness and fatigue
Rare serious bowel inflammation or perforation
Rare serious lung or skin reactions; vision changes

purpose: Treatment aims to slow or shrink lung cancer and relieve symptoms after previous chemotherapy. Expected benefit, side effects, other options and your priorities guide the decision.
schedule_summary: Docetaxel 75 mg/m² is infused on Day 1 every 21 days. For this NSCLC indication, the NCCP plan has a maximum of six cycles; treatment stops earlier for progression or unacceptable side effects. Your team confirms your prescribed dose and course.

consent_support: Discuss treatment aim, alternatives including supportive care, uncertainty, serious and lasting effects, fertility and contraception, premedication, IV access and the urgent contact plan. Explain the six-cycle NSCLC maximum and the possibility of stopping earlier.
urgent_extra: Call the oncology contact number immediately for fever, shivers or sudden illness, severe or new breathing difficulty, chest pain, fainting, severe abdominal pain or persistent diarrhoea. Tell staff immediately about infusion symptoms. Report new numbness, weakness, painful skin changes, swelling or visual changes promptly; do not wait for the next cycle.

support.title: Premedication
support.text: Take dexamethasone exactly as prescribed before and after docetaxel. Tell the unit about missed doses before infusion; any alternative needs the prescriber’s decision. Do not double a dose or add another steroid course yourself.

support.title: Nausea, bowel symptoms and pain
support.text: Use your individual anti-sickness and pain plan. Contact the team if symptoms are uncontrolled or you cannot drink. Antihistamines and other support medicines may cause drowsiness; arrange transport if advised.

support.title: Nerves and daily activities
support.text: Report tingling, numbness or weakness early, including effects on buttons, writing, walking or balance. Protect hands and feet and take care with hot surfaces if sensation changes.

support.title: Infection and blood counts
support.text: Each treatment needs its own blood and symptom review. A growth-factor injection may be prescribed after individual risk assessment; follow its separate instructions. Fever or sudden illness needs immediate contact on any day.

questions.q: What benefit is realistic for me and what other options are available?
questions.a: Treatment aims to slow or shrink lung cancer and relieve symptoms after previous chemotherapy. Expected benefit, side effects, other options and your priorities guide the decision. A historical randomised trial found that docetaxel 75 mg/m² every three weeks prolonged survival compared with supportive care alone in selected people whose NSCLC had progressed after platinum chemotherapy. Modern previous treatment and available alternatives differ, so the trial cannot predict an individual outcome.

questions.q: What are my confirmed infusion days, dose and planned review points?
questions.a: Docetaxel 75 mg/m² is infused on Day 1 every 21 days. For this NSCLC indication, the NCCP plan has a maximum of six cycles; treatment stops earlier for progression or unacceptable side effects. Your team confirms your prescribed dose and course.

questions.q: Who arranges and reviews my blood tests and scans?
questions.a: FBC, kidney and liver profile at baseline and before every 21-day cycle; review symptoms, neuropathy, fluid retention and the steroid plan. Confirm remaining cycles against the six-cycle NSCLC maximum. Ask the team who books each test and who checks the result.

questions.q: What premedication and anti-sickness plan should I follow?
questions.a: Follow the written plan for your exact prescription. Report missed premedication before infusion; confirm prevention and rescue medicines with the pharmacist.

questions.q: Which symptoms need an immediate call, and which number should I use?
questions.a: Call the oncology contact number immediately for fever, shivers or sudden illness, severe or new breathing difficulty, chest pain, fainting, severe abdominal pain or persistent diarrhoea. Tell staff immediately about infusion symptoms. Report new numbness, weakness, painful skin changes, swelling or visual changes promptly; do not wait for the next cycle. Keep the unit’s daytime and out-of-hours numbers on your treatment card.

evidence.title: Why this treatment may be chosen
evidence.intro: A historical randomised trial found that docetaxel 75 mg/m² every three weeks prolonged survival compared with supportive care alone in selected people whose NSCLC had progressed after platinum chemotherapy. Modern previous treatment and available alternatives differ, so the trial cannot predict an individual outcome.
evidence.population: NCCP 00203a: locally advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer after failure of prior chemotherapy. This is docetaxel alone; a platinum or other partner needs its own regimen.
evidence.interpretation: Discuss possible benefit, alternatives and uncertainty for your own situation. The treatment aim is cancer control and symptom relief.
evidence.limitations: TAX317 was a historical randomised study after platinum chemotherapy; it predates current targeted therapy and immunotherapy. The 75 mg/m² cohort followed an initial 100 mg/m² cohort; preserve the dose-specific comparison and do not combine them as one 75 mg/m² estimate. NCCP limits this NSCLC course to six cycles. Trial results are population averages, not an individual survival prediction. TAX320 compared docetaxel with vinorelbine/ifosfamide; its overall survival comparison did not reach statistical significance. Do not imply all comparators showed the same result.

chapters.title: Checks through treatment
chapters.intro: Your team arranges tests, reviews results and confirms each dose.

items.title: Blood tests and symptoms
items.text: FBC, kidney and liver profile at baseline and before every 21-day cycle; review symptoms, neuropathy, fluid retention and the steroid plan. Confirm remaining cycles against the six-cycle NSCLC maximum.

items.title: Heart and breathing
items.text: Assess cardiac history and symptoms; this monotherapy source does not prescribe routine serial echocardiograms. New breathlessness, chest pain or fainting needs assessment.

items.title: Response review
items.text: The consultant agrees when scans and other disease checks are due. New or worsening symptoms may need assessment sooner. There is no automatic fixed scan interval in this regimen.

chapters.title: Practical support
chapters.intro: Bring your medicine list and symptom record to every review.

items.title: Medicines and vaccines
items.text: Check new prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines, supplements and vaccine timing with the oncology pharmacist. Interactions and changes in organ function can alter the treatment plan.

items.title: Fertility and contraception
items.text: Discuss fertility preservation before treatment where relevant. Ask for written contraception and breastfeeding advice for your actual product and the period after treatment. Tell the team promptly about a possible pregnancy.

items.title: Support and priorities
items.text: Ask about symptom control, nutrition, rehabilitation, emotional support and help at home. Review how the treatment burden and possible benefit fit your priorities.

day_groups.body: Docetaxel 75 mg/m² by IV infusion on Day 1 every 21 days. Duration depends on the cancer and treatment aim: NSCLC has a source maximum of six cycles; other indications require an explicitly agreed course, including prostate treatment. This differs from the 100 mg/m² card.

sections.title: Before the visit
sections.text: Check the oral steroid schedule, blood-test appointment and transport. Contact the unit before attending if premedication was missed or you are unwell.

sections.title: At the unit
sections.text: Docetaxel is given through a cannula or suitable existing IV line over about one hour. The appointment also includes checks, preparation, premedication and observation and is longer than the infusion itself. This regimen has no routine take-home pump.

sections.title: At home
sections.text: Keep the contact number, medicine list and symptom record available. Ask who will arrange your next blood test, scan and review. Sedating medicines may affect driving.
